    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.BilinearForm.Diagonalization, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Diagonalization of symmetric bilinear forms in every characteristic #

    Over a commutative ring, an orthogonal basis gives a diagonal Gram matrix and reduces divisibility of all pairings to divisibility of its diagonal values. For a symmetric form with 2 invertible, it also identifies the associated quadratic form with the weighted sum of squares of its self-pairings. The hyperbolic plane can therefore have an orthogonal basis only when 2 is a unit. Over a local ring with 2 invertible, a pairing dividing every value can be replaced by a self-pairing with the same property. A symmetric form with unit Gram determinant has an orthogonal basis with unit self-pairings over any such local ring.

    Over a field in which 2 is invertible, every symmetric bilinear form on a finite-dimensional space has an orthogonal basis (LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_orthogonal_basis); in matrix terms, every symmetric matrix is congruent to a diagonal one. In characteristic two this fails: a nonzero alternating form is symmetric, and an orthogonal basis for it would make every basis pairing vanish, hence the whole form. This file shows that the alternating forms are the only obstruction, in every characteristic: a symmetric form has an orthogonal basis if and only if it is zero or not alternating (LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_orthogonal_basis_iff).

    For a nondegenerate form over a field in which every element is a square, for instance a finite field of characteristic two (isSquare_of_charTwo'), the orthogonal basis can be rescaled: a symmetric form that is not alternating has an orthonormal basis, one in which its matrix is the identity (LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_basis_toMatrix_eq_one). Hence it is equivalent to the standard form Matrix.toBilin' 1, which is itself such a form in every positive dimension (Matrix.isAlt_toBilin'_one_iff in LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.BilinearForm), and any two such forms of the same dimension are equivalent. Together with the symplectic normal form of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.LinearAlgebra.BilinearForm.SymplecticBasis this gives the dichotomy for nondegenerate forms that are alternating or symmetric: a symplectic basis when the form is alternating, an orthonormal basis when it is not (LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.exists_basis_toMatrix_eq_J_or_toMatrix_eq_one). Over 𝔽₂, where every form that is alternating is symmetric, this classifies the nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms, which is the input to the normal forms of one-relator pro-2 groups.

    Gram determinants transform by the square of the coordinate-map determinant. Consequently, the Gram determinants of equivalent bilinear forms differ by the square of a unit, and their product is a square, without symmetry or nondegeneracy assumptions. When 2 is invertible, symmetric bilinear forms are equivalent exactly when their associated quadratic forms are equivalent.

    Main results #

    • LinearMap.BilinForm.iIsOrtho.toMatrix_eq_diagonal: the Gram matrix in an orthogonal basis is the diagonal matrix of its self-pairings.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_iIsOrtho: an orthogonal basis identifies the associated quadratic form with a weighted sum of squares.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.det_toMatrix_comp, LinearMap.BilinForm.det_toMatrix_eq_det_sq_mul_det: the Gram determinant under a linear map and under a change of basis.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.Equivalent.exists_det_eq_unit_sq_mul_det: equivalent forms have Gram determinants differing by a unit square, in any finite bases with the same index type.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.Equivalent.isSquare_det_mul_det: hence the product of their Gram determinants is a square.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.equivalent_iff_toQuadraticMap_equivalent: when 2 is invertible, equivalence of symmetric bilinear forms is equivalent to equivalence of their quadratic forms.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.iIsOrtho.dvd_apply: divisibility from diagonal values.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.isUnit_two_of_iIsOrtho_toBilin'_hyperbolic: an orthogonal basis of the hyperbolic plane forces 2 to be a unit.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_forall_apply_self_dvd_of_forall_dvd: over a local ring with 2 a unit, a minimal pairing yields a minimal self-pairing.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_orthogonal_basis_isUnit_of_isUnit_det: over a local ring with 2 a unit, a unit Gram determinant gives an orthogonal basis with unit self-pairings.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_isUnit_det: such a form is isometric to a unit diagonal quadratic form, with a determinant change-of-basis equation.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_orthogonal_basis_of_isAlt_imp_eq_zero: a symmetric form that is zero or not alternating has an orthogonal basis, in every characteristic.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_orthogonal_basis_iff: this condition is also necessary.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_basis_toMatrix_eq_one: over a field in which every element is a square, a nondegenerate symmetric form that is not alternating has an orthonormal basis.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.equivalent_toBilin'_one, LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.equivalent_of_finrank_eq: such a form is equivalent to the standard form on Fin n → K, so any two of them of the same dimension are equivalent.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.exists_basis_toMatrix_eq_J_or_toMatrix_eq_one: the symplectic-or-orthonormal dichotomy.
    • Matrix.IsSymm.exists_isUnit_transpose_mul_mul_eq_diagonal: when 2 is invertible in a field, every symmetric matrix over it is congruent to a diagonal matrix.

    References #

    • A. A. Albert, Symmetric and alternate matrices in an arbitrary field, I, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 43 (1938), 386–436.
    • O. T. O'Meara, Introduction to Quadratic Forms, 92:1.
    • J. W. S. Cassels, Rational Quadratic Forms, Chapter 8.

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.iIsOrtho.toMatrix_eq_diagonal {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} {b : Module.Basis ι R M} (hb : B.iIsOrtho ⇑b) :
    (toMatrix b) B = Matrix.diagonal fun (i : ι) => (B (b i)) (b i)

    The Gram matrix in an orthogonal basis is the diagonal matrix of the self-pairings.

    The quadratic form of a symmetric bilinear form in an orthogonal basis is isometric to the diagonal form of its self-pairings.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.det_toMatrix_comp {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {N : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (c : Module.Basis ι R N) (C : LinearMap.BilinForm R N) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    ((toMatrix b) (C.comp f f)).det = ((LinearMap.toMatrix b c) f).det ^ 2 * ((toMatrix c) C).det

    Pulling back a bilinear form along a linear map multiplies its Gram determinant by the square of the coordinate-map determinant. The source and target bases use the same arbitrary finite index type; no symmetry or nondegeneracy is required.

    source

    ((toMatrix c) B).det = (b.toMatrix ⇑c).det ^ 2 * ((toMatrix b) B).det

    A change of basis multiplies the Gram determinant by the square of the basis-change matrix determinant.

    Along an orthogonal basis, a common divisor of the diagonal values of a bilinear form divides every value of the form.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.isUnit_two_of_iIsOrtho_toBilin'_hyperbolic {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {ι : Type u_3} {b : Module.Basis ι R (Fin 2 → R)} (hb : (Matrix.toBilin' !![0, 1; 1, 0]).iIsOrtho ⇑b) :
    IsUnit 2

    If the hyperbolic plane, the form with Gram matrix !![0, 1; 1, 0] on R², has an orthogonal basis, then 2 is a unit in R. So over a ring such as ℤ_2 the hyperbolic plane is not diagonalizable.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_forall_apply_self_dvd_of_forall_dvd {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} [IsLocalRing R] (hB : B.IsSymm) (h2 : IsUnit 2) {u w : M} (h : ∀ (y z : M), (B u) w ∣ (B y) z) :
    ∃ (x : M), ∀ (y z : M), (B x) x ∣ (B y) z

    Over a local ring in which 2 is a unit, if a value B u w of a symmetric bilinear form divides every value of the form, then so does one of the self-pairings B u u, B w w and B (u + w) (u + w).

    A symmetric form with unit Gram determinant over a local ring with two invertible has an orthogonal basis with unit self-pairings. The input basis is arbitrary.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_isUnit_det {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} [IsLocalRing R] (hB : B.IsSymm) (h2 : IsUnit 2) {n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) R M) (hdet : IsUnit ((toMatrix b) B).det) :
    ∃ (w : Fin n → Rˣ), (BilinMap.toQuadraticMap B).Equivalent (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R w) ∧ ∃ (d : R), ∏ i : Fin n, ↑(w i) = d ^ 2 * ((toMatrix b) B).det

    A symmetric form with unit Gram determinant over a local ring with two invertible is isometric to a unit diagonal form. The product of its coefficients equals the original Gram determinant times the square of a change-of-basis determinant.

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_orthogonal_basis_of_isAlt_imp_eq_zero {K : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V} [FiniteDimensional K V] (hB : B.IsSymm) (h : B.IsAlt → B = 0) :
    ∃ (v : Module.Basis (Fin (Module.finrank K V)) K V), B.iIsOrtho ⇑v

    A symmetric bilinear form that is zero or not alternating has an orthogonal basis, in every characteristic. Away from characteristic two the hypothesis is automatic for symmetric forms (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.eq_zero_of_isSymm_of_isAlt), which recovers LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_orthogonal_basis; in characteristic two it excludes exactly the nonzero alternating forms.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_orthogonal_basis_iff {K : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V} [FiniteDimensional K V] (hB : B.IsSymm) :
    (∃ (v : Module.Basis (Fin (Module.finrank K V)) K V), B.iIsOrtho ⇑v) ↔ B.IsAlt → B = 0

    A symmetric bilinear form has an orthogonal basis if and only if it is zero or not alternating. The forward direction is the observation that an orthogonal basis of an alternating form pairs every two basis vectors to zero.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.exists_basis_toMatrix_eq_one {K : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V} [FiniteDimensional K V] (hsq : ∀ (a : K), IsSquare a) (hB : B.IsSymm) (hnd : B.Nondegenerate) (h : B.IsAlt → B = 0) :
    ∃ (v : Module.Basis (Fin (Module.finrank K V)) K V), (toMatrix v) B = 1

    A nondegenerate symmetric form that is not alternating has an orthonormal basis, over a field in which every element is a square: rescaling an orthogonal basis by inverse square roots of the self-pairings makes the matrix of the form the identity. The hypothesis on squares holds in every finite field of characteristic two (isSquare_of_charTwo').

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.equivalent_toBilin'_one {K : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V} [FiniteDimensional K V] (hsq : ∀ (a : K), IsSquare a) (hB : B.IsSymm) (hnd : B.Nondegenerate) (h : B.IsAlt → B = 0) :
    B.Equivalent (Matrix.toBilin' 1)

    Over a field in which every element is a square, a nondegenerate symmetric form that is not alternating is equivalent to the standard form ∑ i, x i * y i on Fin n → K, for n the dimension.

    Over a field in which every element is a square, two nondegenerate symmetric forms that are not alternating, on spaces of the same dimension, are equivalent.

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.exists_basis_toMatrix_eq_J_or_toMatrix_eq_one {K : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V} [FiniteDimensional K V] (hsq : ∀ (a : K), IsSquare a) (hnd : B.Nondegenerate) (h : B.IsAlt ∨ B.IsSymm) :
    (B.IsAlt ∧ ∃ (m : ℕ) (v : Module.Basis (Fin m ⊕ Fin m) K V), (BilinForm.toMatrix v) B = Matrix.J (Fin m) K) ∨ ¬B.IsAlt ∧ ∃ (v : Module.Basis (Fin (Module.finrank K V)) K V), (BilinForm.toMatrix v) B = 1

    The normal-form dichotomy for a nondegenerate form that is alternating or symmetric, over a field in which every element is a square: an alternating form has a symplectic basis, and a symmetric form that is not alternating has an orthonormal basis. In characteristic two every alternating form is symmetric, so the hypothesis is just symmetry there.

    theorem Matrix.IsSymm.exists_isUnit_transpose_mul_mul_eq_diagonal {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Field K] [Invertible 2] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n K} (hA : A.IsSymm) :
    ∃ (P : Matrix n n K) (d : n → K), IsUnit P ∧ P.transpose * A * P = diagonal d

    A symmetric matrix over a field in which 2 is invertible is congruent to a diagonal matrix: Pᵀ * A * P is diagonal for some invertible P. This is the matrix form of LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_orthogonal_basis.
